subject: Seat decommissioning & migration sprint plan: GitHub/JetBrains renewal window
messages:
From: Alex Liu <alex.liu@acme.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal timing + inactive seat clean-up for GitHub & JetBrains

Hi Maya,

We're approaching our Nov renewal window for both GitHub Enterprise and JetBrains seats. We ran the usage extract (attached) and it looks like ~120 seats across the org are effectively unused for >=9 months. Procurement asked whether Redwood can help with a staged downgrade/migration so we don't pay full list on renewal.

High level ask: can Redwood provide programmatic seat decommissioning guidance + recommended cadence for moving idle seats to a lower tier or license retirement prior to our renewal date (2026-12-01)? Also, any pointers on how vendor counting works (seat pooling vs active user metrics) for your recommended approach would help our finance team.

Attached: GHE-usage-report-Oct2026.csv

Thanks,
Alex Liu
IT Procurement
Acme Systems

Date: 2026-11-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + inactive seat clean-up for GitHub & JetBrains

Alex — thanks for the data and the clear ask. We can absolutely help; happy to run a short sprint with your team to identify candidates for retirement and set up a safe migration path.

Proposed next steps: 1) quick kickoff call this week to align on scope and SLA; 2) run the seat-mapping & API-based idle-user disable in a staging project (we'll provide scripts); 3) schedule a one-week cutover (rolling) to move seats off paid SKUs or reassign to active contributors.

Can you confirm your renewal cutoff date (you mentioned Dec 1) and whether you need us to coordinate directly with JetBrains/GitHub billing? If yes, include the account execs on thread.

I'm looping in Karthik (platform & procurement coordination) to weigh in on implementation timeline.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: seat decommissioning sprint — timeline & checklist

Team — quick internal note after Maya looped me in. I'd propose the following sprint cadence for Acme:

- Day 0 (Nov 8): Kickoff + confirm renewal dates and vendor counting rules.
- Day 1-3: Run usage analysis + tag candidate accounts for decommission.
- Day 4-7: Staging script to disable/repurpose seats (preserve repos/artifacts).
- Day 8-12: Pilot window with 20-30 seats; monitor CI/CD and access errors.
- Day 13-20: Roll remaining seats in two waves.

Risks: repo access regressions, missed service accounts, license overcounting in vendor portal. Mitigations: backup service accounts list, repo-level access audits, vendor validation call pre-cutover.

I attached a rough checklist — we should refine and make vendor-facing.

Attachment: seat-migration-checklist.xlsx

Karthik
Head of Platform Partnerships

Hi Maya / Alex,

Thanks for the heads up. Attached is our quote for the tier-reduction path and a short note on how JetBrains counts active users when evaluating renewals. Key points:
- We can provide a one-time pro-rated credit for seats retired within 30 days before renewal (subject to account review).
- Service accounts are normally excluded from active-user counts if tagged; please confirm tagging approach.
- We recommend a 7-day pilot to validate license reductions.

Thanks all — summary and agreed next steps:

1) Kickoff call: Nov 8, 10:00 PT — attendees: Acme procurement, Acme IT lead, Redwood platform (Karthik, Maya), Renewals (Marissa).
2) Scope: identify ~120 idle seats from GHE report; tag service accounts; run staging script and pilot 30 seats Nov 15-17.
3) Vendor coordination: JetBrains confirmed pro-rated credit option; GitHub exec looped in for validation.
4) Cutover waves: Nov 20-21 (wave 1), Nov 24-25 (wave 2). Rollback: re-enable seats from backup list within 24 hours if access errors >1%.

Deliverables: MAP doc (Marissa to draft), migration checklist (Karthik to finalize), vendor sign-off (Elena / GitHub exec) before Nov 15.

Alex — is procurement OK with the two-wave cutover and pilot dates? If yes we'll send calendar invites and vendor join links.

Best,
Maya
